summary: Mount-dead chain-load failure aborts the run immediately (non-zero) instead of burning to --max, per spec/RELEASE-v0.7.md §4

per.section: 4. Exit-code contract — the run never lies to CI

edit.description: Per the operator's §4 amendment: the load/mount failure class (~L483-499) gets its own distinct exit constant (sibling to EX_TERMINAL_MISCONFIG at L372 — not a TickOutcome field); superviseLoop (~L1718-1784) aborts on that code and continues on a plain tick-failure code, mirroring the existing EX_TERMINAL_MISCONFIG fail-fast branch.
tickExitCode (~L130-133) and loop's exit mapping (~L771-777) route the new signal to abort; HELP_SUB tick/loop prose (~L199-220) updated to match.
Add bullet under Added per §13.

Rewrite the ungated-resolution-failure scenario (~L2995-3023, today asserts continue-not-abort) to assert abort-on-first-mount-dead-occurrence — a semantics change to an existing assertion, not new coverage, per §4.
Rewrite tickExitCode({failed:true}) expectation (~L204-212) to the new mount-dead exit value.
Update hibernation/--max cases for the revised contract.

tests.asserts: superviseLoop aborts non-zero on first mount-dead tick instead of burning to maxTicks.
an unloadable chain exits non-zero after one tick's worth of work; an empty-queue run exits 0.
loop process boundary exits correctly for hibernation and --max cases under the revised contract.

acceptance: A run against an unloadable chain exits non-zero after one tick's worth of work; an empty-queue run exits 0.
notes: Ratified by the operator's 2026-07-29 §4 amendment: distinct mount-dead exit constant, and cli.test.ts:211 / Dispatcher.test.ts:2995 rewrite is explicitly authorized (they lock behavior this section supersedes) — not build's call anymore, not scope creep. Shipped/errored counting split to EXIT-CODE-CONTRACT-COUNTS, blocked on this.

summary: loop/job run exits 0 with errors named when ≥1 tick errored but ≥1 entry shipped, per spec/RELEASE-v0.7.md §4

per.section: 4. Exit-code contract — the run never lies to CI

edit.description: superviseLoop's only per-iteration signal is the child's exit code (stdio: inherit, ~L1795-1813) — add a small per-tick disk artifact (disk-is-truth) the supervisor reads between iterations to recover shipped/errored counts; exit non-zero iff ≥1 tick errored AND 0 entries shipped.
loop/job run completion summary names surfaced errors even on a zero exit (partial success).
Add bullet under Added per §13.
a run with one errored tick and one shipped entry reports shipped>0 and errored>0, exits 0, error named in summary.
same scenario surfaces correctly at the CLI/loop boundary.

tests.asserts: run with one errored tick + one shipped entry: exit 0, shipped>0, errored>0, error named.
same scenario surfaces correctly at the CLI/loop boundary.

acceptance: A run with one errored tick and one shipped entry exits 0 and its summary names the error.
notes: Design ratified by the operator's 2026-07-29 §4 amendment: exit codes carry class only (settled/errored/mount-dead); a per-tick disk artifact carries counts. Child stdio stays inherit — piped-and-parsed stdout is explicitly declined (live-streamed agent output is load-bearing).

summary: Detect CJS-context chain-load failure and refuse with usage-shaped message per spec/RELEASE-v0.7.md §5

edit.description: loadChainModule (src/Dispatcher.ts:234-274): catch tsx module-context signature family (tsx 4.21 'Cannot use import statement outside a module'; tsx 4.23 ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND with tsImport '?namespace' percent-encoded) and rethrow a distinguishable usage-shaped error naming "type": "module" as the fix, per §5. Non-matching errors pass through unchanged (no false positives).

Surface the usage-shaped CJS-context refusal as exit 2, consistent with other usage errors and with the EXIT-CODE-CONTRACT taxonomy this entry rides on top of. Underlying loader error stays available as debug/verbose detail, not the headline.
Add bullet under [Unreleased] Fixed.

tests.asserts: loadChainModule against the two known tsx CJS-context signatures (4.21 and 4.23 shape) throws the usage-shaped refusal naming "type": "module"; a genuinely missing dependency's error passes through unchanged.
chain load in a CJS-context fixture prints the usage-shaped refusal and exits 2.

acceptance: Chain load in a CJS-context fixture (the npm init -y smoke shape, pre-fix) prints the usage-shaped refusal naming "type": "module" and exits 2; a genuinely missing dependency still surfaces as itself.
notes: Blocked on EXIT-CODE-CONTRACT: exit 2 must sit consistently alongside that entry's mount-dead/errored-vs-shipped taxonomy rather than being designed twice. Detection signature is the empirical tsx 4.21/4.23 family from the inbox finding (c11d96b fixed the two known fixture instances by adding type:module; this entry makes the failure legible generically, not just those two fixtures).

summary: repoRoot walks up from cwd to the nearest .flume, mirroring git's .git resolution, per spec/RELEASE-v0.7.md §9

edit.description: Replace the literal repoRoot = process.cwd() (~L515) with a walk-up resolver per §9: cwd-is-.flume special case, no-.flume-found fallback to today's behavior, FLUME_DIR/FLUME_CONFIG_DIR overrides unchanged.
Add bullet under Added per §13.
Cover: subdirectory-below-bay invocation resolves the same repoRoot as bay root; invocation from inside .flume; no .flume anywhere above cwd keeps cwd-as-root.

tests.asserts: cd .flume && flume job status resolves the same bay as running from repo root (no false 'no jobs'); a tree with no .flume anywhere above keeps today's cwd-as-root default.

acceptance: cd .flume && pnpm flume job status (or any subcommand) resolves the same bay as running from the repo root; a tree with no .flume anywhere above it keeps today's cwd-as-root default.

summary: Global bin re-execs a bay's local install when present, refuses loudly when pinned-but-absent, per spec/RELEASE-v0.7.md §10

per.section: 10. Engine↔pin handshake via launcher-defers-to-pin (the gradlew pattern)

edit.description: Before subcommand dispatch: three arms per §10 — local install at <bay>/.flume/node_modules/@dtmd/flume resolves → re-exec its CLI with the same argv/stdio; pinned in package.json but install absent → refuse exit 2 naming pin + readPackageVersion() (~L53-60); unpinned → unchanged.
Adjust only if the arms can't live entirely inside src/cli.ts's entry — build's call which site hosts the re-exec.
POSIX sibling; same caveat as bin/flume.js.
Add bullet under Added per §13.
Version-stamped smoke fixtures distinguishing local vs global install per §10 acceptance.

tests.asserts: bay with local install present → any invocation re-execs it regardless of global version; local install removed on a pinned bay → refuses exit 2 naming pin + both versions; unpinned bay → byte-identical to today.

acceptance: A bay with the local install present re-execs it regardless of the global engine's version; the same bay with the local install removed refuses (exit 2) naming the pin and both versions; an unpinned bay behaves byte-identical to today.
notes: Reuses the existing win32-junction link machinery job new already provisions as the resolution signal — not redesigned. One hop only. Hosting site (cli.ts main() vs bin/ shims) is build's call; all candidate files declared so either choice stays in-fence.

summary: Ship a pnpm/npm lockfile-aware setupWorktree helper; migrate the dogfood chain onto it, per spec/RELEASE-v0.7.md §11

new.description: New exported helper, sibling to builtinGates.ts's shellGate/tscGate precedent: pnpm-lock.yaml → pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; package-lock.json → npm ci; neither → refuse cleanly, per §11.
New test file asserting lockfile-detection behavior per §11.

edit.description: Re-export the new helper alongside the existing builtinGates re-exports (~L30-37).
Replace buildSetupWorktree (~L95-103) with the new helper — dogfood discipline.
Rewrite the setupWorktree worked example (~L418-458), currently teaching hardcoded pnpm install, to show the new helper as the recommended default.
Add bullet under Added per §13.

tests.asserts: pointed at a pnpm-lock.yaml fixture dir runs pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; pointed at a package-lock.json fixture dir runs npm ci; pointed at neither refuses cleanly.

notes: Non-goals per spec: yarn/bun lockfile support; migrating connect's own chain.ts (that repo's own follow-up, outside this entry's blast radius).
